title: Requirements for a successful collision
body: In most reactions only a small fraction of collisions leads to a reaction; a successful collision has both of the following.

items.label: Sufficient energy
items.meaning: enough energy to overcome the activation energy requirements

items.label: Suitable orientation
items.meaning: an orientation that allows the bonds to rearrange in the required manner

caution: The CED says that in most reactions only a small fraction of collisions is successful. Do not state that all collisions, or all energetic collisions, produce products.
ced_evidence: 5.5.A.2 "Successful collisions have both sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy requirements and orientations that allow the bonds to rearrange in the required manner."

title: Types of catalysis named in the CED
body: The CED names three ways that some catalysts accelerate a reaction, and each typically introduces new intermediates and elementary reactions.

items.label: Binding to reactant(s) (5.11.A.3)
items.meaning: the catalyst binds the reactant(s), which are oriented more favorably or react with lower activation energy; there is often a new intermediate with the catalyst bound to the reactant(s); many enzymes function this way

items.label: Covalent bonding between catalyst and reactant(s) (5.11.A.4)
items.meaning: an example is acid-base catalysis, in which a reactant or intermediate gains or loses a proton; this introduces a new intermediate and new elementary reactions involving it

items.label: Surface catalysis (5.11.A.5)
items.meaning: a reactant or intermediate binds to, or forms a covalent bond with, the surface; this introduces elementary reactions involving the new bound intermediate(s)

caution: The CED says 'some catalysts' work each way and that a new intermediate is 'often' present. Do not make these universal statements about all catalysts.

title: Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution
body: A distribution curve of particle energies, used to gain a qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react and how that fraction depends on temperature.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: relative number (fraction) of particles having each energy

items.label: Distribution curve
items.meaning: describes the distribution of particle energies at a given temperature

items.label: Activation energy marker
items.meaning: a vertical line on the energy axis; particles at or above it have sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy

items.label: Area beyond the marker
items.meaning: qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to lead to a reaction

items.label: Curves at different temperatures
items.meaning: show how the fraction of sufficiently energetic particles depends on temperature

caution: The CED treats this as a qualitative estimate only. Energy alone is not enough, because successful collisions also need a suitable orientation.
ced_evidence: 5.5.A.3 "The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve describes the distribution of particle energies"
